fields.meta_description: Create a waitlist landing page from a prompt, with places in line, referral links, invite batches, and a database you own. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Waitlist Landing Page for Your Next Launch
fields.hero_description: Build a waitlist landing page that shows each signup a place in line and saves every email to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Comes With Each Waitlist Page
fields.features_subheading: Visitors see a short form and their place in line. These six parts cover what sits behind them, through to the code you keep.
fields.feature_1:
A waitlist page written from one prompt

Describe the product, who it is for, and when it opens. Emergent builds the page, the signup form, and the waitlist table behind them, and changes any part when you prompt again.
fields.feature_2:
A place in line for every signup

Each person who joins sees a number and a link to share. You decide how many spots one referral is worth, and the confirmation email repeats the number for anyone who closes the tab.
fields.feature_3:
Signups in a database you own

Each signup is a row in a database you own, with the date, the answers, and the link that brought it. Send those rows to HubSpot or any tool with an API instead of exporting a file.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts for the signups that matter

Choose the signups that deserve a person's attention, such as a team of 50 or more. The page posts each one to Slack or emails the founder who will follow up on it the same day.
fields.feature_5:
A signup count that updates live

The counter on the page and the dashboard behind it update as each signup arrives. Split the count by source or by test version to see which link or headline brings people in.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain today, the code later

Publish the page on your own domain, which is included and uses credits. On paid plans, the full code exports to your GitHub repository, ready for the launch site that comes next.

fields.tab_content_1:
Every friend who joins moves you up 10 spots

Quillfern, an invoicing app for freelancers, gives everyone who joins a number in line and a referral link. Each friend who joins through it moves the link's owner up 10 spots. Odessa Fennick joined at #1,482. Three friends used her link, and she now sits at #1,452. Referrals save to the waitlist table.
fields.tab_content_2:
Clinics with 10 or more therapists skip the line

Cobaltine, scheduling software for physical therapy clinics, sends 200 invites every Monday at 9 AM. Its early access form asks how many therapists a clinic has, and clinics with 10 or more skip ahead to the next batch. Tamberlane Physio signed up with 14 therapists, and founder Lennart Sefton got a Slack message.
fields.tab_content_3:
The first 150 in line get 24 hours to claim a mug

Harrow Clay Studio fires one spring run of 150 mugs, and 412 people joined its waitlist, each picking a glaze. On release day, the first 150 get a claim link that holds a mug for 24 hours. A mug left unclaimed passes to #151, then on down the line. Cordelia Abernathy, #38 on the list, claimed hers in oat glaze.
fields.tab_content_4:
Half of visitors see $8 a month, half see $12

Marguerite Corvell put up a landing page MVP for Pantrywise, a meal planner, before building it. The page splits visitors evenly between the two prices and saves each signup with its price. After 1,000 visitors, 500 per price, the $8 page had 61 signups. The $12 page had 47, both counted live on her dashboard.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Waitlist Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Follow these seven steps to publish a waitlist landing page that numbers every signup and lets people in on a schedule.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write the promise in one line
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Pick the rule that moves people up
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Describe the page in a prompt
fields.howto_step_1_des: Say what the product does, the person it is made for, and when the first invites go out. That line becomes the headline. If you cannot name a month yet, say how invites will work instead, such as weekly batches in signup order.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask for an email and at most one more answer you will act on, such as team size or role. Cut any field you would not use to order the list. Ask for a name later, in the invite email, when people have a reason to give it.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Choose referrals or priority. With referrals, each friend who joins moves the person who shared the link up a set number of spots; with priority, an answer such as team size moves a signup forward. Write the number down now: the page and the email will both state it.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Paste the promise, the fields, and the rule into one prompt. Emergent returns a working page with its form, the place-in-line logic, and the waitlist table. Prompt again for the confirmation screen: it should show the new number and the referral link.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Connect the email tool that sends the confirmation, then Slack for the signups you want to hear about as they arrive. If sales will follow up with larger teams, map those rows to your CRM now instead of copying them by hand later.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Sign up with one address, then join twice through its referral link with two others. Check that the first address moved up by the right number of spots, that each confirmation email arrived, and that all three rows sit in the table.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Publish and set the first batch date
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish the page and share the link where your first users already spend time. Set the date and size of the first invite batch before the list grows, put both on the page, and email the list the same day.

faq_plan.q: What is a waitlist landing page?
faq_plan.a: A waitlist landing page is a single page that collects the email addresses of people who want a product before it is ready. It says what is coming and when, asks for an email, and can show each person their place in line. When the product opens, that list becomes the first group you invite.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a waitlist landing page?
faq_plan.a: Describe the product, the form fields, and the rule for moving up the list to Emergent's AI landing page builder in a few sentences. Read the first version as a visitor would, top to bottom. Then join once yourself and check that your row lands in the table with the right number before you share the link.

faq_plan.q: What should a landing page MVP test?
faq_plan.a: It should test one question you cannot answer from your desk: whether people want the product enough to leave an email, or what price they will accept. Write the pass mark down before launch, such as 40 signups from 800 visitors. A result below it counts as a no.

faq_plan.q: What should I copy from waitlist landing page examples?
faq_plan.a: Copy what a visitor needs at a glance: a headline that names the product and who it is for, one email field, and a line on when invites go out. Skip a countdown clock that has no date. If the page only announces a date with a notify-me box and no line behind it, a coming soon page fits better.

faq_plan.q: How do I stop fake signups on a waitlist form?
faq_plan.a: Ask each person to confirm their email address before the signup counts, and assign the place in line only after they click. On a referral list, count a friend only once their address is confirmed, which stops one person climbing with throwaway accounts. Forms built with Emergent have no response cap, and a list that doubles overnight keeps every confirmed signup.

faq_plan.q: What happens after people join the waitlist on a landing page?
faq_plan.a: They land on a confirmation screen that shows their place in line and the link to share. After that, write only when there is news, such as the date of the first invite batch. When you announce the launch, the FTC's CAN-SPAM guide says your message must include your valid physical postal address. Put it in the footer of every update.

faq_plan.q: What are some MVP landing page examples?
faq_plan.a: A fake-door page offers a feature that does not exist yet and counts the clicks on its button. A concierge page promises the service done by hand for the first 10 customers and takes their names. If search will bring the visitors, plan the landing page SEO before launch. Emergent builds either page from a prompt, and the free tier covers building and publishing it.

faq_plan.q: How many people should an early access landing page invite at once?
faq_plan.a: Invite as many as you can onboard well in a week. If one person answers every support question, start with 20 to 50 and raise the batch when the questions slow down. State the schedule on the page, and people waiting will know when the next group goes out.

faq_plan.q: Should an early access form ask qualifying questions?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if the answers decide who gets in first. Put a line next to the question that says it affects timing: a person invited after a larger team then knows why. Keep the same questions for every batch, and the answers stay comparable across the whole list.

faq_plan.q: Can a waitlist signup form work for a service business?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Any business with more demand than capacity can use one: a clinic with a full calendar, a class that sells out, or a practice taking new clients slowly. A law firm landing page, for example, can take names for a free consultation day that is already booked and invite people in signup order as slots open.
